text: Two nights before the Derby, his mother was at a big party in town when a rush of anxiety about her boy gripped her heart till she could hardly speak. <break time="0.8s" /> She hurried home late that night and, creeping upstairs, heard from her sons room a strange, heavy, and yet not loud noise that made her heart stand still. <break time="0.8s" /> When she switched on the light, she saw her son in his green pajamas, madly surging on the rocking horse, and he screamed in a powerful, strange voice, It is Malabar. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he fell to the ground with a crash, and he remained unconscious with a brain fever, tossing and talking, while his mother sat stonily by his side. <break time="0.8s" /> After the Derby, Bassett came softly into the sickroom and told the boy, Malabar came in first all right, a clean win, and you have made over seventy thousand pounds. <break time="0.8s" /> Opening his blue eyes, the boy said to his mother, Mother, did I ever tell you, If I can ride my horse and get there, then I am absolutely sure. <break time="0.8s" /> I am lucky, he said, and his mother answered softly, No, you never did, but the sick boy did not recover, and he passed away quietly in the night. <break time="0.8s" /> As she sat beside her son for the last time, the mother heard her brothers voice saying, Hester, you are eighty odd thousand to the good, and a poor son to the bad. <break time="0.8s" /> But, poor boy, he is best gone out of a life where he rides his rocking horse to find a winner.
